correctness.rationale: For each finite-horizon deterministic adapted rule, divide its exact Beta-binomial winning probability by all-failures probability to obtain a finite sum of strictly A-increasing and B-decreasing rising-factorial ratios. Finiteness and endpoint limits prove the unique increasing acceptance root. The first-future-success policy gives universal odds upper line. Simultaneous induction through success and failure posterior updates proves optimality throughout B>=k(k-1)+1 beneath the line. At odds equality below that bound, postponing selection on the next observed success strictly improves success probability. For k=2 solving the two possible future policies gives the stated square-root/linear minimum. All domains and tie cases are covered; 1181 independent exact finite assertions (including exhaustive future-policy enumeration for k<=4) support but do not replace the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected motivating primary work gives posterior backward recursions and warns of nonmonotone sample-path behavior, not the explicit all-horizon necessary-and-sufficient quadratic parameter region and strict low-shape separation. Searches of published mathematical findings under Bayesian last-success, odds, Beta-binomial, posterior threshold and equivalent/parameter forms did not reveal this implication. Standard finite dynamic programming is not itself considered original; the motivated sharp phase boundary is the new object. Risk remains of classical equivalent Bayesian stopping formulations.
residual_risks: Classical Bayesian secretary or last-success literature may encode the same quadratic boundary under another formulation.
The potentially relevant Paindaveine preprint and related 2026 stopping literature were not available in complete full text.
A public mathematical research index is a search aid, not an exhaustive uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The motivated question is whether Bayesian updating destroys the familiar first-success odds rule: Ano 2026 finds pathwise nonmonotonicity, while a sharp tractable posterior region was not given. The result classifies the exact necessary-and-sufficient high-failure-shape region for all finite horizons and exhibits strict low-shape adaptive improvement; the nontrivial quadratic k(k-1)+1 crossover and exact two-trial root directly guide stopping decisions and reveal where posterior learning changes qualitative policy. It is substantially more than re-evaluating an isolated finite Bellman table.
